subject: Interim region-binding: KMS toggle and short telemetry hop request
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@medstream.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Short-term analytics hop and region-binding question

Hi David,

Quick question from our infra and security teams as we run a migration: we need to perform a one-time analytics sweep over a newly onboarded EU tenant. The analytic job runs in our US analytics cluster and will pull anonymized telemetry for 48–72 hours for model evaluation.

Can Redwood: 1) confirm that our customer data will remain region-bound (EU) except for this explicitly authorized transient hop, and 2) provide a mechanism to temporarily toggle KMS to allow the analytics job to decrypt telemetry in the US for that window, with auditability and automatic re-lock after the window?

We need a short operational playbook and a DPA addendum outlining the temporary exception, plus an assurance that logs/audit trails are captured and retained per GDPR. Legal cc'd.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call today.

—Sarah
Senior PM, MedStream Health

[no attachments]
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@medstream.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term analytics hop and region-binding question

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: we can support a documented, time-boxed transient egress for telemetry with KMS controls, but we need to align on scope and approvals. A few clarifying questions so our runbook and DPA addendum are precise:

- Scope: what exact telemetry fields are required (IDs, IPs, event types, PHI?); if anything is sensitive we must ensure pseudonymization before transit.
- Window: you mentioned 48–72 hours. Confirm the start timestamp and whether you need a 24h buffer for pre/post verification.
- Decryption: do you want Redwood to perform the KMS toggle (we'll record and sign the action), or will MedStream provide a short-lived key access?
- Audit: we'll include token-level audit logs, KMS key rotation events, and a tamper-evident record exported to your legal S3. Confirm retention period.

I've looped in Kimberly and Marcus from Product/Infra to draft the playbook and a technical design for the KMS toggle, and Marissa for the DPA amendment language. We can put together:

1) A two-page Ops playbook (start/stop checklist, verification, rollback)
2) A KMS toggle design doc (access gating, operator approvals, automated rollback)
3) Short DPA addendum describing the temporary exception, data minimization, and retention of audit evidence

Are you available for a 30-min call today at 3pm PT? If not, we'll draft the artifacts and send for your legal review.

Best,
David
Director, Account Solutions — Redwood Inference

[no attachments]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@medstream.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term analytics hop and region-binding question

Hi all —

Attaching an initial tech design and a skeletal playbook for the transient KMS toggle and telemetry hop. High-level notes below; full details in attachments (kms-toggle-design.pdf, transient-egress-playbook.docx).

- Principle: region-bind by default. Temporary egress is explicitly authorized per request, time-boxed, and must be operator-approved with two-person control.

- KMS flow (proposed):
  * Customer data remains encrypted at rest in EU with customer-scoped keys.
  * For the approved window, a temporary key-unwrap operation is performed by Redwood infra. We do NOT export long-term plaintext; plaintext exists only in ephemeral memory on the analytics worker and is zeroed after job termination.
  * All key-unwrapping operations are gated by our Operator Approval workflow (two approvers) and logged in KMS audit trails.

- Telemetry minimization: we strongly recommend stripping unique identifiers prior to transit. If MedStream cannot provide pseudonymized exports, Redwood will run an additional scrubbing step (adds ~2 hours to prep).

- Audit & retention: we will produce:
  * KMS access log (signed),
  * per-request token tracing for processed objects, and
  * an export bundle (read-only) to a customer-controlled S3 with SHA256 digests for integrity.
  * Default retention for audit artifacts is 90 days; can extend on request.

- Failure modes & rollback: automatic re-lock after the window; any anomalies trigger an immediate halt and an incident runbook.

Next steps: Marcus to confirm infra capacity and scheduling constraints; Marissa will propose DPA addendum text for Legal review. Sarah: if you can confirm telemetry fields and the proposed start window (including buffer), we'll finalize the playbook and DPA text and route for signatures.

Thanks — attaching artifacts.

—Kimberly
Sr Product Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms-toggle-design.pdf (diagram + approvals table), transient-egress-playbook.docx (runbook, verification checklist)
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@medstream.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: MedStream Legal <legal@medstream.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Short-term analytics hop and region-binding question

Kimberly / David —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear design. Confirming:
- Telemetry fields: event_type, event_timestamp, anonymized_user_hash (no PII, no IPs).
- Window: target start 2027-05-03T02:00:00Z for a 72-hour run; we want a 12-hour pre-check window and 24-hour post-verification period.
- Retention: audit artifacts for 180 days preferred.

We'll sign the DPA addendum once Marissa shares the draft. Attached is our PO for the transient work (MedStream_PO_0427.pdf).

Please proceed with scheduling the prep run the week before the start date. Legal — please let us know if you need any additional language for the addendum.

Thanks,
Sarah
Senior PM, MedStream Health
